resources.string: The frame is on (%1$s). Tap to hide it. Hold for its shapes and margins.
Show the frame (%1$s): where the picture\'s edges are. Hold for its shapes and margins.
The director\'s chair: Scene, Character and Shots on the strip
Scenes: the empty scene and yours. Tap one to change scene.
Who is in the scene. Tap one to take it in hand.
Shots: where the camera is. They need the frame.
The empty scene: the plain stage with one character. It is where you are. Tap again to arrange the character on it.
%1$s is in hand: your fingers and voice move them. Tap again (or hold) to set them up.
%1$s. Tap to go there; hold (or tap it again) to set it up.
Keep the view the camera has now as a shot
The camera eases to the shot
How the camera goes to a shot
Kept as “%1$s”. Hold its card to name it.
Where the picture\'s edges are. It only shows them: nothing on the stage moves.
The classic margins: keep action inside the cyan line and words inside the pink one
About where an app lays its own buttons and words over an upright video. Every app differs: treat it as a guide.
The earlier way: a margin all round, so a character part-way out is still on the screen. Off, the frame is as big as the screen allows.
Changing the shape moves nothing: the frame is a window on the same stage. Export cuts the picture to it. This is the empty scene\'s frame; each scene keeps its own.
Keep the view as a shot
Your shot. To frame it again, close this, drag the empty stage or pinch, then use the view.
This shot is worked out by itself. To make your own: close this, drag the empty stage or pinch, then keep the view.
